candidates.source: Titolo and Palmisano, From Villages to Empires, South Levant, doi10.5281/zenodo.15111732
candidates.exposure: New metadata/README/changelog only before this declaration
candidates.finding: Candidate with explicit survey polygons, site-phase records, quality codes and Late Roman70–324AD category. Broad-period compatibility includes AD200 but does not establish simultaneous AD200 occupancy or dated phase-specific area.

selected_for_input_qualification: South Levant, chosen for published polygon support, phase fields, quality codes and directly accessible archived GIS, before reading model outcomes.
canonical: Pinned dataset.gpkg. Cross-check CSV and record every discrepancy: latest source commit fixes GPKG SizeHa. Never overwrite a source file or silently merge disagreeing versions.
scope: Read source README/license/field descriptions/GPKG/CSV plus associated scholarly methods for this SAME third candidate. Qualify CRS, survey polygon meaning and overlap, site/phase identity, date conventions, type/quality and source linkage. No source software execution. Site-phase rows are not independent towns or a population census.
observation_contract: Prefer a conditional spatial-presence comparison within independently supplied survey polygons at a scale the existing model supports. Define any Late Roman phase selection and settlement-type inclusion from source semantics BEFORE scoring. Do not use all-region bounding box, site-derived buffers or convex hull as survey area. Preserve holes, overlaps, zero observations and unknown survey attribution; no new detection probability is inferred.
phase_and_area: Source Late Roman70–324AD is a broad site-phase presence proxy. Do not call it an AD200 census. SizeHa is not automatically occupation-specific built-up area or population. Derive no inhabitants from size. Caves/tombs/features cannot be treated as towns without explicit type handling.
score_gate: No model predictions or scores before a separate committed cohort/support/metric declaration and independent input review. If polygon/support/type/phase semantics fail, record a limited contract or refusal rather than manufacturing validation.
deliverable: Three-source eligibility table, exact source provenance/hash receipt, independent input-contract review and one observation contract. If spatial support qualifies, continue with a separately frozen same-support simple baseline comparison.
protected: Keep the current published r5 and Roman benchmark qualification/source/output files unchanged. New data exposure is documented; historical regional geometry overlap prevents an automatic independent-geographic or blind-validation claim.
exclusions: No refit, hierarchy tuning, new work/food/climate/route solver, warehouse research, population estimate, atlas adoption or reserved Buringh/workbook opening.
